summary: Full-extraction pass over 20 stored US documents: the DOJ Civil Division FCA statistics (FY2024 and FY2025 editions), the GSK 2012 off-label settlement agreement, eleven DOJ press releases on large qui tam settlements and the UBS/Swiss Bank tax cases, the DOJ Swiss Bank Program page and an OSHA Wells Fargo retaliation order. Main addition: every remaining cell of the FY2024 FCA statistics edition (1,352 rows); the FY2025 edition was already complete and was checked cell by cell. Also 9 qui tam cases (GSK settlement agreement, HCA sub-settlements, J&J sub-settlements), 10 cumulative FCA recovery figures and 1 event.

observations.location: p. 1, table "Fraud Statistics - Overview", row FY1987, column "New matters - non qui tam"

observations.location: penultimate paragraph (HEAT initiative)
observations.quote: the FCA, which the Justice Department has used to recover almost $2.8 billion since January 2009 in cases involving fraud against federal health care programs
observations.notes: Cumulative from January 2009 to the date of the release (period end = release date). Rounded figure as printed; whistleblower and non-whistleblower FCA cases together. "almost": rounded up.

observations.location: penultimate paragraph (HEAT initiative)
observations.quote: The Justice Department’s total recoveries in FCA cases since January 2009 are over $3.75 billion.
observations.notes: Cumulative from January 2009 to the date of the release (period end = release date). Rounded figure as printed; whistleblower and non-whistleblower FCA cases together. "over": rounded down.

observations.location: paragraph beginning "This settlement is part of the government's emphasis"
observations.quote: the False Claims Act, which the Justice Department has used to recover approximately $4.2 billion since January 2009 in cases involving fraud against federal health care programs
observations.notes: Cumulative from January 2009 to the date of the release (period end = release date). Rounded figure as printed; whistleblower and non-whistleblower FCA cases together. "approximately".

observations.location: paragraph beginning "This settlement is part of the government's emphasis"
observations.quote: The Justice Department's total recoveries in False Claims Act cases since January 2009 have topped $5.4 billion.
observations.notes: Cumulative from January 2009 to the date of the release (period end = release date). Rounded figure as printed; whistleblower and non-whistleblower FCA cases together. "topped": rounded down.

observations.location: last paragraph (HEAT initiative)
observations.quote: the False Claims Act, which the Justice Department has used to recover more than $7.4 billion since January 2009 in cases involving fraud against federal health care programs
observations.notes: Cumulative from January 2009 to the date of the release (period end = release date). Rounded figure as printed; whistleblower and non-whistleblower FCA cases together. "more than": rounded down.

observations.location: last paragraph (HEAT initiative)
observations.quote: With the settlement announced today, the Justice Department's total recoveries in False Claims Act cases since January 2009 will exceed $10.2 billion.
observations.notes: Cumulative from January 2009 to the date of the release (period end = release date). Rounded figure as printed; whistleblower and non-whistleblower FCA cases together. "will exceed": includes the Abbott settlement announced that day; rounded down.

observations.location: paragraph beginning "One of the most powerful tools"
observations.quote: Since January 2009, the Justice Department has recovered a total of more than $16.7 billion through False Claims Act cases
observations.notes: Cumulative from January 2009 to the date of the release (period end = release date). Rounded figure as printed; whistleblower and non-whistleblower FCA cases together. "more than": rounded down.

observations.location: paragraph beginning "One of the most powerful tools"

observations.location: last paragraph (HEAT initiative)

cases.whistleblower: Greg Thorpe; Blair Hamrick; Thomas Gerahty; Matthew Burke; Lois Graydon; Michael LaFauci
cases.summary: Civil settlement of four qui tam actions in D. Mass. (ex rel. Thorpe; ex rel. Gerahty; ex rel. Graydon; ex rel. LaFauci) over off-label promotion of and kickbacks for Paxil, Wellbutrin, Advair, Lamictal, Zofran and kickbacks for Imitrex, Lotronex, Flovent and Valtrex: $1,042,612,800 plus interest (federal $832,485,436; Medicaid participating states $210,127,364). The agreement leaves the relators' share open.
cases.quote: GSK agrees to pay to the United States and the Medicaid Participating States, collectively, the sum of one billion, forty-two million, six hundred twelve thousand, eight hundred dollars ($1,042,612,800)
cases.notes: Quote from OCR of the scanned agreement. Allocation by drug (p. 7): Paxil $52,622,130; Wellbutrin $166,979,130; Advair-Asthma $686,049,841; Advair-COPD July 2008-June 2010 $25,273,910; Lamictal $54,729,862; Zofran $2,320,640; kickbacks $54,637,287 (sums to the total). Interest at 1.625% a year from 1 Dec 2011 on top. Relator names are as printed in the case captions and signature pages (Hamrick and Burke appear only on signature pages). Effective date is the last signature (not printed legibly; signature dates in June 2012); the DOJ release on this resolution is dated 2 July 2012 (cases c-a84d604404, c-ddce0c7731 describe the whole $3 billion resolution). The agreement says it does not cover the relators' claims to a share under 31 U.S.C. 3730(d).

cases.summary: HCA cost-report fraud qui tam lawsuits (Medicare, Medicaid, TRICARE): $356 million, plus $20 million of the settlement toward separately pursued cost-reporting allegations of the same relators. The two relators receive $100 million in total as their statutory share.
cases.location: paragraph "$356 million to resolve whistleblower lawsuits..."
cases.quote: In total, the two relators are to receive a total of $100 million as their statutory share of the settlement.
cases.notes: Award is the two relators combined. Whether the $20 million is inside the $356 million is not clear from the release. Part of the HCA settlement announced 26 June 2003 whose total ($631 million; whistleblowers $151,591,500 combined) is already case c-45df0336a3; do not add the two together. Relators named by DOJ in the release.

cases.whistleblower: James Thompson; Gary King; Ann Mroz
cases.summary: HCA kickback qui tam lawsuits (illegal remuneration to physicians for referrals; Medicare, Medicaid, TRICARE): $225.5 million. Relator shares: Dr. James Thompson $41.5 million (statutory share), Gary King $5 million, Ann Mroz a share of $837,500.
cases.location: paragraph "$225.5 million to resolve lawsuits alleging..."
cases.quote: Dr. James Thompson, a doctor who filed suit against the company in 1995, will receive $41.5 million as his statutory share of the settlement.
cases.notes: award_amount left empty: three relators with separate amounts and no combined figure printed. Part of the HCA settlement announced 26 June 2003 whose total ($631 million; whistleblowers $151,591,500 combined) is already case c-45df0336a3; do not add the two together. Relators named by DOJ in the release.

cases.summary: HCA hospitals billed Medicare for unallowable wound-care-center contractor costs and a non-covered drug: $17 million. Joseph "Mickey" Parslow receives $2,990,000 and Francesco Lanni a share of $680,000. The contractor (Curative Healthcare Services) had earlier paid $16.5 million in the same lawsuits.
cases.quote: Joseph "Mickey" Parslow, a former HCA financial officer, will receive $2,990,000 and Francesco Lanni
cases.notes: award_amount left empty: two relators with separate amounts and no combined figure printed. Part of the HCA settlement announced 26 June 2003 whose total ($631 million; whistleblowers $151,591,500 combined) is already case c-45df0336a3; do not add the two together. Relators named by DOJ in the release.

cases.summary: HCA allegedly shifted home office costs to hospitals: $950,000 settlement; relator Michael Marine receives a share of $116,500.
cases.location: paragraph "$950,000 to settle allegations made by Michael Marine"
cases.quote: Marine will receive a share of $116,500.
cases.notes: Part of the HCA settlement announced 26 June 2003 whose total ($631 million; whistleblowers $151,591,500 combined) is already case c-45df0336a3; do not add the two together. Relators named by DOJ in the release.

cases.summary: Separate agreement: HCA pays $1.5 million over kickbacks for diabetes-patient referrals at West Paces Medical Center, Atlanta, in U.S. ex rel. Pogue v. American Healthcorp, Inc. et al., a case the United States declined to join. Pogue receives a share of $405,000.
cases.location: paragraph "In a separate agreement, HCA agreed to pay $1.5 million"
cases.quote: Pogue, a former employee of a co-defendant in the case, Diabetes Treatment Centers of America, will receive a share of $405,000 from the HCA settlement.
cases.notes: Declined (non-intervened) qui tam. First name not given in the release. Separate from the $631 million settlement (c-45df0336a3), but the $405,000 is probably inside the $151,591,500 combined figure (not stated).

cases.target: Johnson & Johnson; Janssen Pharmaceuticals (Risperdal and Invega)
cases.summary: Off-label marketing and kickbacks for Risperdal and Invega: $1.273 billion in this resolution (federal $749 million, states $524 million), part of $1.391 billion including $118 million paid to Texas in March 2012. Whistleblowers in E.D. Pa. receive $112 million from the federal share.
cases.location: paragraphs "As part of the global resolution, J&J and Janssen have agreed to pay a total of $1.391 billion" and "From the federal government’s share"
cases.quote: the whistleblowers in the Eastern District of Pennsylvania will receive $112 million
cases.notes: Matched to the Risperdal/Invega settlement because the release says that civil complaint was filed in E.D. Pa. Part of the J&J resolution already recorded as c-6de6a184aa ($1.72 billion civil); do not add together.

cases.summary: Kickbacks to Omnicare to promote Risperdal and other J&J drugs in nursing homes: $149 million (federal $132 million, five states $17 million). Whistleblowers in D. Mass. receive $27.7 million from the federal share.
cases.location: paragraphs "J&J and Janssen have agreed to pay $149 million" and "From the federal government’s share"
cases.quote: the whistleblowers in the District of Massachusetts will receive $27.7 million
cases.notes: Matched by district: the release says the Omnicare complaint was filed in D. Mass. (January 2010). Part of c-6de6a184aa; do not add together.

cases.summary: Off-label marketing of Natrecor for serial outpatient infusions: $184 million to the federal government. The whistleblower in N.D. Cal. receives $28 million from the federal share.
cases.location: paragraphs "J&J and Scios have agreed to pay the federal government $184 million" and "From the federal government’s share"
cases.quote: the whistleblower in the Northern District of California will receive $28 million
cases.notes: Matched by district: the release says the Natrecor complaint was filed in N.D. Cal. (2009). Part of c-6de6a184aa; do not add together.

events.title: Court authorises IRS "John Doe" summons on UBS
events.description: The U.S. District Court in Miami authorised the IRS to serve UBS a John Doe summons for records identifying U.S. taxpayers with concealed UBS accounts in Switzerland (the same month Birkenfeld pleaded guilty). Day not given.
events.location: paragraph beginning "In June 2008, former UBS private banker Bradley Birkenfeld"
events.quote: Also, in June 2008, the U.S. District Court in Miami authorized the Internal Revenue Service to serve upon UBS a so-called "John Doe" summons

ledger.contains: DOJ Civil Division 'Fraud Statistics - Overview, October 1, 1986 - September 30, 2024' (12 pp.): four tables (Overview; HHS; DoD; Other non-HHS/non-DoD), each by fiscal year FY1987-FY2024 plus a TOTAL row, with 10 columns: new matters non qui tam and qui tam; settlements and judgments non qui tam, qui tam where U.S. intervened or otherwise pursued, qui tam where U.S. declined, qui tam total, total; relator share awards intervened, declined, total. Notes define new matters, settlements (incl. common law recoveries), relator shares (exclude 3730(h) claims) and the FY2020 series break (U.S. Attorneys' Office matters added to non qui tam). Already in the data: 208 cells (the cells the FY2025 edition revised, plus most FY2024 cells). Added: the other 1,352 cells, so all 1,560 cells (156 rows x 10 columns, including the four cumulative TOTAL rows, period FY1987-FY2024) are now recorded; notes say whether the FY2025 edition prints the same or a different figure. Checks: count columns add up exactly (intervened + declined = qui tam total; non qui tam + qui tam = total; year rows sum to TOTAL; HHS + DoD + Other = Overview). Dollar columns differ by $1 to $3 in many rows and totals, which is rounding in the source.

DOJ Civil Division 'Fraud Statistics - Overview, October 1, 1986 - September 30, 2025' (16 pp.): same four tables (Overview, HHS, DoD, Other), FY1987-FY2025 plus TOTAL row, same 10 columns and notes (numbered 0-3 in this edition). Already in the data: all 1,600 cells (40 rows x 10 columns x 4 tables, including TOTAL rows as FY1987-FY2025). This pass re-read every cell from the PDF and found no differences with the recorded values. Nothing added. Checks as for the FY2024 edition: counts add up exactly; dollar columns differ by $1 to $3 (rounding in the source).

Scanned settlement agreement (34 pp., read by OCR) between the United States, relators and GlaxoSmithKline LLC resolving four qui tam actions in D. Mass. (ex rel. Thorpe; ex rel. Gerahty; ex rel. Graydon; ex rel. LaFauci): covered conduct (off-label promotion and kickbacks for Paxil, Wellbutrin, Advair, Lamictal, Zofran; kickbacks for Imitrex, Lotronex, Flovent, Valtrex); settlement amount $1,042,612,800 plus 1.625% interest from 1 Dec 2011, allocated by drug (adds up to the total), split federal $832,485,436 / Medicaid participating states $210,127,364; releases, excluded claims, unallowable costs, dismissal terms; the relators' share under 3730(d) is expressly left open; signature pages (DOJ, HHS-OIG, TRICARE, OPM, GSK, relators Thorpe, Hamrick, Gerahty, Burke, Graydon, LaFauci and counsel). Nothing from it was in the data. Added: 1 case (allocation by drug in its notes).

DOJ press release 12-842 (2 July 2012), GSK $3 billion resolution: criminal plea ($1 billion: fine $956,814,400, forfeiture $43,185,600; Paxil/Wellbutrin $757,387,200; Avandia $242,612,800); civil settlements: off-label and kickbacks $1.043 billion (federal $832 million, states $210 million) resolving four qui tam suits in D. Mass.; Avandia $657 million (federal $508 million, states $149 million) and price reporting $300 million ($160,972,069 federal, $118,792,931 states, $20,235,000 Public Health Service entities), neither linked to a qui tam suit in the release; corporate integrity agreement; HEAT: more than $10.2 billion over three years in health care fraud under the FCA and the FDCA combined (fines and forfeiture included, so not an FCA recovery figure; not recorded). No relator share is printed. Already in the data: 1 case and 1 event. Nothing added (the off-label qui tam settlement is now also a case from the settlement agreement itself). Same release as usa-doj-pr-gsk-2012 (another capture); both already have a case row for the same resolution.

DOJ press release 10-1205 (26 Oct 2010): SB Pharmco Puerto Rico (GSK) plea over adulterated drugs from the Cidra plant; $150 million criminal fine and forfeiture (incl. $10 million forfeiture); $600 million civil FCA settlement (federal $436,440,000, states up to $163,560,000) resolving one qui tam suit; whistleblower Cheryl Eckard receives about $96 million; HHS-OIG quote on nearly $2.3 billion pharmaceutical settlements in FY2010 (HHS-OIG figure, not an FCA total; not recorded); FCA recoveries since January 2009 (about $4.2 billion health care, over $5.4 billion total). Already in the data: 1 case and 1 event. Added: 2 cumulative FCA recovery observations.

DOJ press release (2 Sep 2009), Pfizer $2.3 billion: criminal fine $1.195 billion and forfeiture $105 million ($1.3 billion criminal); $1 billion civil FCA settlement (federal $668,514,830, state Medicaid $331,485,170) over Bextra, Geodon, Zyvox, Lyrica; qui tam suits in D. Mass., E.D. Pa., E.D. Ky.; six whistleblowers receive more than $102 million; corporate integrity agreement; officials' quotes (USPS 'more than $1 billion' workers' compensation, not programme). Already in the data: 1 case and 1 event. Nothing added. Same release as usa-doj-pr-pfizer-2009 (another capture); both already have a case row for the same settlement.

DOJ press release (7 May 2012), Abbott $1.5 billion over Depakote: criminal fine $500 million, forfeiture $198.5 million, $1.5 million to Virginia MFCU; civil settlements $800 million (federal $560,851,357, states $239,148,643) resolving four qui tam suits in W.D. Va.; whistleblowers receive $84 million; CIA; HEAT: FCA recoveries since January 2009 (more than $7.4 billion health care; over $10.2 billion total) and $3.9 billion FDCA criminal fines etc. (not FCA, not recorded). Already in the data: 1 case. Added: 2 cumulative FCA recovery observations.

Extracted once, under usa-doj-gsk-pr-2012 and the settlement agreement. Already in the data: 1 case (duplicates the case from usa-doj-gsk-pr-2012). Nothing added.

DOJ press release 03-386 (26 June 2003), HCA: $631 million civil settlement of nine qui tam suits (D.D.C.); earlier $840 million criminal/civil (Dec 2000); $250 million CMS administrative settlement; $1.7 billion total; whistleblowers $151,591,500 combined (record); sub-settlements: cost reports $356 million (Alderson and Schilling $100 million), kickbacks $225.5 million (Thompson $41.5 million, King $5 million, Mroz $837,500), wound care $17 million (Parslow $2,990,000, Lanni $680,000; Curative earlier $16.5 million), patient transfers $5 million, Lawnwood $5 million, home office costs $950,000 (Marine $116,500); separate $1.5 million Pogue declined case ($405,000); states $17.5 million; 2001 criminal fines $22.6 million and $30 million. The listed sub-settlements ($609.45 million) do not add up to 'nearly $620 million' and the named shares do not add up to $151,591,500; the release does not explain. Already in the data: 1 case and 1 event. Added: 5 cases (cost reports, kickbacks, wound care, Marine, Pogue). Transfers and Lawnwood not separate cases (no relator named).

DOJ press release (4 Nov 2013), J&J more than $2.2 billion: Janssen plea $400 million (fine $334 million, forfeiture $66 million); Risperdal/Invega civil $1.273 billion (federal $749 million, states $524 million; $1.391 billion with $118 million paid to Texas in 2012); Omnicare kickbacks $149 million (federal $132 million, states $17 million; Omnicare paid $98 million in 2009); Natrecor $184 million (Scios 2011 fine $85 million); whistleblowers E.D. Pa. $112 million, D. Mass. $27.7 million, N.D. Cal. $28 million; CIA; FCA recoveries since January 2009 (more than $16.7 billion; more than $11.9 billion health care); FDCA more than $6 billion since 2009 (not FCA, not recorded). Added: 3 cases (one per civil settlement, matched to the whistleblower payment by district) and 2 cumulative FCA recovery observations.

DOJ press release 09-038 (15 Jan 2009), Eli Lilly $1.415 billion over Zyprexa: criminal fine $515 million, forfeiture $100 million; civil up to $800 million (federal $438,171,544; states up to $361,828,456) resolving four qui tam actions in E.D. Pa. (ex rel. Rudolf, Faltaous, Woodward, Vicente, all former Lilly sales reps); relators receive $78,870,877; earlier $62 million state consumer-protection settlements (not programme). DOJ press release (27 Apr 2016), Wyeth and Pfizer $784.6 million over Protonix best-price reporting (federal $413,248,820, state Medicaid $371,351,180); relators Lauren Kieff and William St. John LaCorte (U.S. ex rel. Kieff and LaCorte v. Wyeth, D. Mass.); relator share $98,058,190; FCA recoveries since January 2009 (more than $29 billion; more than $17.5 billion health care). Already in the data: 1 case. DOJ press release (27 Jan 2016): final Category 2 Swiss Bank Program NPA (HSZH Verwaltungs AG, penalty $49.757 million; 605 U.S.-related accounts, peak about $1.12 billion); 80 banks, more than $1.36 billion penalties since 30 March 2015; programme announced 29 Aug 2013; UBS DPA history; IRS OVDP penalties 27.5% / 50% and 54,000 taxpayers paying more than $8 billion (voluntary disclosure, not whistleblower). Context for the UBS/Birkenfeld IRS award only; no whistleblower numbers. Already in the data: 1 case and 2 events. Nothing added.

Context for the UBS case only.

DOJ press release 09-tax-136 (18 Feb 2009), UBS deferred prosecution agreement; the stored copy is readable and has the same text as usa-doj-ubs-dpa-pr-2009 (an older capture; the source note saying nothing was read refers to the blocked live download). Contents listed under usa-doj-ubs-dpa-pr-2009. Extracted once there. Nothing added.

DOJ press release (18 Feb 2009), UBS DPA: $780 million in fines, penalties, interest and restitution; disclosure of U.S. client identities under a FINMA order; exit from undeclared U.S. business; 2000 qualified-intermediary agreement; about 3,800 banker trips to the U.S. in 2004 (about the crime, not the programme); Raoul Weil indicted Nov 2008 (not programme); Birkenfeld plea June 2008; John Doe summons authorised June 2008. No whistleblower award mentioned. Already in the data: 1 case and 1 event. Added: 1 event (John Doe summons).

DOJ press release (21 Feb 2020): Wells Fargo $3 billion (DPA, FIRREA civil settlement, SEC cease-and-desist incl. $500 million civil penalty for investors) over 2002-2016 sales practices; statement-of-facts summary. No whistleblower or award in the release. Already in the data: 1 case and 1 event. Nothing added.

Protection, not a reward. Already in the data: 1 case and 1 event. Nothing added.
